plan.topic: Flying with your tirzepatide pen for Thanksgiving: carry-on vs checked bag, keeping it in its original labelled box, and storage limits as the label states them
plan.angle: Sentence 1: 'Flying with your tirzepatide pen? Here's what the label says about storage.' By 6 s, tagged to the Zepbound PI (28 Aug 2026) and the pen IFU's own URL: don't freeze, keep it in the original carton to protect it from light, and the unrefrigerated time and temperature limit exactly as printed. TSA line only as tsa.gov prints it, with its live date (medicines allowed in carry-on; tell the officer about liquid medicines). Untagged tip: 'Many people keep it in their carry-on so they can control how it's stored, in its original labelled box.' Untagged: 'Unsure if a pen is still OK? Ask your pharmacist.' Scope card: US pens; UK/AU packs and KwikPens may differ. No missed-dose or skip-a-dose talk, no dates in narration.

plan.why: The radar shows travelling with the pen as rising with low competition ahead of Thanksgiving travel week. It starts the holiday series on the curve, and it's about flying, not the 11-15 fridge-storage question. | fact-check: The topic is safe and timely. Tighten sentence 1, though: 'Carry-on or checked bag matters' reads like a sourced claim, but neither the label nor TSA says checked bags damage pens. The safe facts are: the label says don't freeze and protect from light, the label gives an unrefrigerated limit (check the time and temperature at the live PI/IFU URL, with no rounding), and TSA allows medicines in carry-ons. Carrying the pen yourself is our own tip, so it must be untagged and framed as 'so you can control how it's stored'. Thanksgiving belongs only in the post copy and the series log, never as a date in narration. Keep the scope card for US vs UK/AU packs and KwikPens.

social.instagram_caption:
Flying with your tirzepatide pen this Thanksgiving? 🦃

That "wait, how do I pack this" moment before a trip is so normal. Here's what the US label says:

→ If needed, a single-dose pen can stay unrefrigerated up to 21 days total, no warmer than 86°F (30°C)
→ Don't freeze it, or use it if it's been frozen
→ Keep it in the original carton to protect it from light

And from TSA: medically necessary liquids are allowed in carry-ons. Declare it to officers at the checkpoint.

Our tip: keep the pen in your carry-on, in its labelled box, so you're the one controlling how it's stored.

KwikPens and packs outside the US may differ. Unsure if a pen is still OK? Ask your pharmacist.

Save this before your next trip ✈️

factcheck.summary: This Short can ship. I checked all three sources and the facts hold up. The Mounjaro label (section 16.2 on DailyMed, revised 27 Aug 2026) says the single-dose pen or vial can be kept unrefrigerated "if needed" at no more than 30°C/86°F, for up to 21 days in total. It also says "Do not freeze MOUNJARO. Do not use MOUNJARO if frozen" and "Store MOUNJARO in the original carton to protect from light." The Zepbound label (DailyMed, revised 28 Aug 2026) has matching storage rules. I could only get a summary of that page, not the exact wording, but it was consistent. It lists single-dose pens, vials and a KwikPen. The TSA page (last updated 15 Apr 2019) says: "TSA allows larger amounts of medically necessary liquids… but you must declare them to security officers at the checkpoint for inspection." Both labels list multi-dose KwikPens and vials, and the Mounjaro label gives them different 30-day rules, so the on-screen note "KwikPens may differ" is correct. I count about 117 spoken words, inside the tight arm. The ending follows the 11-17 Shorts format, with no subscribe line and no "link in the description". The tip in s6 is clearly marked as our own and has no source tag. The title's "Carry-On or Checked?" question is answered by our tip plus the TSA rule. There are four small wording fixes below.

issues.claim: a single-dose pen can stay unrefrigerated up to 21 days
issues.problem: The label says 21 days in total, then throw the pen away. Without 'in total', viewers could think the clock restarts if the pen goes back in the fridge.
issues.fix: Narration: "The US label says, if needed, a single-dose pen can stay unrefrigerated up to 21 days in total." On-screen text: "US single-dose pen: up to 21 days total unrefrigerated, if needed" (+2 words, total about 119).

issues.problem: Captions are built from the on_screen_text field, so the spoken safety line 'Not personal advice, so ask your prescriber.' wouldn't get a caption card. It would appear only in the quote visual. Every safety line has to be both spoken and shown on screen.
issues.fix: on_screen_text: "Not personal advice, so ask your prescriber. Check the carton before flying." (two caption cards, one sentence each; the last card is "Check the carton before flying.")

issues.claim: Visual list: "US single-dose pens" / "Packs outside the US may differ" / "KwikPens may differ"
issues.problem: KwikPens are also sold in the US and have different storage rules (30 days). The first item reads like a statement with nothing to say about it, and the screen says something about KwikPens that the narration never mentions.
issues.fix: Items: "This Short: US single-dose pens" / "US KwikPens and vials: different rules" / "Packs outside the US may differ". Optional narration: "KwikPens and packs outside the US may differ." (+2 words)

issues.claim: TSA allows medically necessary liquids in carry-ons. Declare it to the officer at the checkpoint.
issues.problem: This is accurate, but the TSA page also says the officer has the final say. The on-screen text doesn't name what to declare.
issues.fix: On-screen text: "TSA: declare medicines at the checkpoint" (narration can stay as is).

audio.soundNotes: Music is already sitting at -13.5 dB under voice (within the -12/-15 target) and only needs trimming in a few spots, not a global level change, so gain stays at 1.0. The main fix is thinning stacked/redundant transition pairs (swell+whip, swoosh+whip, swell+whoosh firing at the same timestamp) that were each hitting the same -14 to -15 dB and effectively doubling up; I pulled the second layer down in each case so the transition still reads but doesn't pile on. I also cut an outlier pop that was 7 dB over the speech-SFX ceiling and trimmed one whoosh that was sitting right at the loud edge of the speech window. The quiet 'ghost' cues (swell/tick near -35 to -55 dB) look like a ducking artifact from an earlier pause and are already inaudible, so no action needed there. Added a few bespoke texture hits (airport ambience, a chilled thermometer chime on the 86°F reveal, a bag zip, a paper rustle) to add scene-specific color the stock kit can't give without ever crowding the narration.
